**Gensol Engineering (2025) – fund diversion via related parties**
- SEBI interim order of 15 Apr 2025 barred Gensol and promoters Anmol & Puneet Singh Jaggi from the securities market and from director/KMP roles; case began with a June 2024 complaint about share price manipulation and fund diversion — [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/company-stock/story/sebi-bars-gensol-engineering-its-promoters-from-accessing-markets-in-fund-diversion-case-472151-2025-04-15)
- Gensol took ₹977.75 cr term loans, ₹663.89 cr earmarked for 6,400 EVs (for BluSmart), but only 4,704 vehicles were procured; funds allegedly went to a ₹42.94 cr DLF Camellias apartment and personal spends — [Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/blusmart-crisis-gensol-loans-for-procuring-evs-used-to-buy-dlf-camellias-flat-says-sebi); SEBI order described as "personal piggy bank" — [Moneylife](https://www.moneylife.in/article/how-jaggi-brothers-used-gensol-engineering-as-personal-piggybank-sebi-reveals-in-explosive-order/76903.html)
- Order mentions shell companies, circular fund flows and forged documents; stock split put on hold — [Moneylife](https://www.moneylife.in/article/how-jaggi-brothers-used-gensol-engineering-as-personal-piggybank-sebi-reveals-in-explosive-order/76903.html); [Angel One](https://www.angelone.in/news/sebi-cracks-down-on-gensol-engineering-over-funds-misuse-halts-stock-split)
- Jaggi brothers resigned May 2025; SEBI confirmed the interim order 30 Jul 2025 — [The Week](https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/business/2025/05/12/dcm50-biz-gensol-promoter-resign.html); [The Week](https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/business/2025/07/30/dcm123-biz-sebi-gensol.html)

`case_study:byjus-2022-2024` | 2024-07-16 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Byju's (Think & Learn) was valued at ~$22 bn in 2022, up from ~$5 bn in 2020, after a debt-and-equity-funded acquisition spree (Aakash ~$950 m, WhiteHat Jr ~$300 m, Great Learning, Epic, Toppr). FY21 accounts were filed ~18 months late with a restated loss of ~Rs 4,588 cr after auditor Deloitte forced deferral of upfront revenue recognition; FY22 loss ~Rs 8,245 cr. In Jun 2023 Deloitte resigned (citing delayed statements) and three board members (Prosus, Peak XV/Sequoia, Chan-Zuckerberg) quit. Lenders of a $1.2 bn term loan alleged default and that ~$533 m was moved to a small Miami hedge fund. BlackRock and Prosus cut marks to $11 bn, $5 bn and eventually near zero. Insolvency was admitted in Jul 2024 over BCCI dues; successor auditor BDO resigned in Sep 2024. Visible flags: (1) revenue recognised upfront on EMI-financed courses; (2) aggressive sales practices and refund complaints; (3) late filings and auditor change; (4) founder-controlled board with investors lacking information; (5) leverage via covenant-lite US loan to buy growth. Lesson for IPO-bound/private names: delayed audited accounts, auditor resignations and board exits are disqualifiers regardless of brand; check revenue recognition and CFO vs reported growth.

**Lesson:** Late accounts + auditor exit = walk away
**Spotted early by:** auditor Deloitte; US lenders; journalists (The Ken, Morning Context)
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:disqualifiers`, illustrates -> `insight:auditor-exit-signal`

`person:group-reliance-mukesh` · flag: **mostly-clean** · confidence: verified · tickers: RELIANCE, JIOFIN, NETWORK18, TV18BRDCST, HATHWAY, DEN, JUSTDIAL, ALOKINDS

Flag: MOSTLY-CLEAN. Reliance Industries (promoter ~50%) is the core; subsidiaries Jio Platforms and Reliance Retail were funded with ~$25bn+ of strategic/PE equity (2020) and a Rs 53,124 cr rights issue (2020). No promoter pledging; Jio Financial Services was demerged 1:1 (2023), a clean value-distribution. Regulatory record: SEBI's 2007 RPL share-sale case -- SEBI ordered disgorgement (2017) and in Jan-2021 fined RIL Rs 25 cr and Mukesh Ambani Rs 15 cr for manipulative trading; SAT quashed the 2021 penalty order (Dec-2023) and separately set aside a Rs 25 cr takeover-code penalty on the Ambani family (Jul-2023) citing SEBI's inordinate delay; a report says the Supreme Court later dismissed SEBI's appeal (date unverified). Other concerns: decades of 'opaque structure' criticism (layers of promoter entities), large RPT flows between RIL and subsidiaries, minority buy-outs at subsidiary level (Reliance Retail capital-reduction exit for minorities, 2023), KG-D6 cost-recovery dispute with the government (unresolved; figures not verified here), and the Network18/media group's long losses. Positives: consistent dividends, bonus issues, debt-reduction promises largely met (net-debt-free claim 2020, later re-levered). Status Nov-2026: Jio Platforms IPO reported for Oct-2026 with an RIL-shareholder reservation (one source lists a 21-23 Oct issue at Rs 1,065-1,119; others say H2FY27 -- unconfirmed); watch whether IPO pricing and listing of Reliance Retail treat RIL holders fairly (holdco discount risk).

- **red flags:** 2007 RPL case (penalties later quashed by SAT); opaque promoter layers; subsidiary-level value capture
- **good conduct:** JFS demerger; rights issue at discount to all; no pledges; shareholder reservation in Jio IPO
